The status can say that all eligible troops are ready while time continues until you stop it. Training belongs to the currently open visit; it is not an invisible permanent training order left behind after departure. Escape closes the training visit. Use the visible Train and Stop controls to manage training deliberately. Layout example — Training Yard: choose a trainer, inspect party troops, and watch the training status before stopping.

title: Household pictures and privacy
text: Castle Chat Image Generation controls room scenes independently of general portrait replacement. A room picture illustrates the chosen people and setting; it is not a substitute for their actual presence or a completed action. Family Chambers, Homes, and room chat have different audiences. Before discussing a private matter, check which session you entered and who is selected. Someone else's nearby room is not automatically part of your conversation.

title: Capitals and Rule Mode
text: As ruler, use Designate Capital in an eligible town of your kingdom. At a safe kingdom town or castle, Enter Rule Mode opens court business. The capital provides Royal Court with full royal scope; another eligible holding provides a reduced Local Docket . Captivity, siege, and unsafe conditions can interrupt access. Enable Court System in MCM if the menu is unavailable. A saved setting that turned it off stays off after an update. Owning a castle without ruling a kingdom does not automatically grant full royal authority. The Royal Court's main areas include Court, Court History, Lands, Subjects, Diplomacy, Ambassadors, Spymaster, and Military, with entrances to Government, Royal Council, Family Chambers, and Castle Layout. Use Lands and the Economic Report to investigate a shortage before deciding how to spend the treasury. Escape closes the main Court screen. In a supported conversation opened from court, Alt+A opens actions; it is not a shortcut for every Court tab. The Court window fits itself to your display while keeping its proportions. Recent development work corrects its size on taller displays; check the installed version if yours looks different. Layout example — Royal Court: tabs lead to different kinds of business; your current location and office determine your authority.

title: Hearing and deciding petitions
text: Petitions come from actual needs rather than a queue filled with invented emergencies. Core petitions concern food, town funds, village recovery, and soldiers for security. Read the petitioner, settlement, requested aid, and proposed commitment. Talk with the petitioner, then use the explicit decision: grant direct aid, fund a supported alternative, or refuse. Conversational sympathy alone does not spend the treasury or send soldiers. If you lack the resources, a pending case does not count as fulfilled. Direct soldier aid detaches real troops while protecting a minimum home defence. An expedition can suffer losses and returns through its recorded route or a safe fallback. Gold alternatives can be costly because they fund the replacement work, not merely the face value of a few items. Petitions do not simply vanish because you postponed them. Try this: open a food petition, inspect the affected holding, and compare direct aid with the funded alternative before deciding. Check Court History afterward for the recorded result. In-game screenshot - Court audience: an ambassador presents an International request. Read the request and conversation, then use the separate Review Decisions, Confirm, Refuse Request or Postpone controls. This audience concerns an envoy's offer to fund a friendship ceremony. Talking through an offer and confirming a decision are separate steps; read the final terms before confirming.

title: Noble disputes, visitors, and patronage
text: Preview: broader noble, international, household, visitor, and patronage business exists in the court implementation; it is separate from the certified core relief-petition slice and has further acceptance work. Court life also includes noble disagreements over precedence, insult, scandal, family affairs, property, and more serious misconduct. Hear each actual principal, consider the known evidence, and read the available ruling. A losing side can accept, resent, or resist your judgment. An accusation does not automatically establish the accused behavior or its reputation. Foreign court matters use the relevant international participants and authority. A local household quarrel is not permission to commit another kingdom to a treaty. Native marriage, custody, imprisonment, or death still needs its actual supported game action; conversation cannot bypass it. Noble visitors can make courtesy calls, introduce themselves, or bring family introductions. A reserved visit can temporarily make someone unavailable for an office or other duty. A social introduction is not an accepted marriage. Patronage brings artists and supported commissions into court life. Review the named work, price, and delivery before funding it. Discussion alone does not grant a commissioned work or its benefits; only a properly paid supported commission does. Some audiences provide characterization without a mechanical reward.

title: Chancellor and delegation
text: Ask an eligible person in direct conversation to become Chancellor, agree on pay, and review the appointment. The Chancellor is a capital-resident docket office, separate from the Royal Council seats. It may require leaving an incompatible governorship or field command. Appointment begins inactive. Activation and deactivation take effect at the next scheduled morning docket boundary, rather than immediately rewriting the day. Active service costs its agreed daily salary and suppresses ordinary petitions. Unpaid service cannot continue indefinitely. Delegating often can give you the social appearance of an absent ruler. Captivity has an emergency Chancellor lifecycle and a handoff after release. The old Regent is retired; historical Regent entries do not mean that office still governs your current court.

title: Offices and the Royal Council
text: Court work depends on capable, loyal, trustworthy people as well as skill. Steward, Economic Advisor, Foreign Advisor, Marshal, and Spymaster duties use different talents. Absence and conflicting duties matter. Do not assume appointing the highest visible skill guarantees the best outcome. The Royal Council has War Councilor, Spymaster, Economic Advisor, and Foreign Advisor seats. One person cannot occupy every major seat. Select the War Councilor through the War Council. Economic and Foreign Advisors must be eligible and available for residence at the capital. Ask the relevant advisor for a briefing or a fuller explanation. Advice is advisory: it does not issue a war order, pay a grant, change a treaty, or secretly settle a relationship. Only present participants share that council conversation. Preview: Royal Council residence, briefings, routing, and capital changes have implementation and interface evidence, but their full native/provider acceptance remains open. Layout example — Royal Council: occupied advisor stations surround the shared transcript; advice still needs your separate decision.

title: Economic reports and court supply
text: Open the Economic Report to inspect the realm's condition, including food and military burdens. Hover food information for reserve and projected-shortage explanations. Compare actual village output with healthy output; a town's full market is not the same as its settlement food reserve. Court transfers require actual stock, money, a valid route, and the necessary ownership or consent. A negotiated shipment is not free food. Spent resources and incoming cargo must be accounted for before you assume another grant is affordable. If workshop or caravan profit is marked unmeasured, read that as unavailable ledger information rather than zero earnings. See Economy and survival for how population, relief, and military costs interact. In-game screenshot - Economic Report: compare settlement information on the left, prepare a transfer request in the middle, and review the kingdom overview, military logistics and Economic Advisor on the right. Read the report date; displayed amounts belong to this campaign.

title: Your kingdom's institution
text: Government represents organized political members and constituencies alongside the ruler and noble pressures. Its parties have platforms, members, speakers, coalitions, and differing interests. Government trust is different from personal friendship or Public Standing. Institution Typical representation Imperial Senate Town and village notable constituencies Great Council of Peers Qualifying landholding clans Grand Veche Landholding clans and town merchant/artisan constituencies Oenach Landholding clans and village headman/landowner constituencies Majlis al-Shura Landholding clans and town merchant constituencies Great Kurultai Qualifying landholding clans Great Thing Landholding clans and town/village notable constituencies Council of Estates Landholding clans and town notable constituencies Use Royal Court → Government for the ruler view. Castle Layout → Government also provides the supported public view; viewing it does not make you ruler. A new kingdom's Founding Charter lets the player review the institution and its starting authority. Confirming a charter is a constitutional choice, not a cosmetic culture selector. Existing kingdoms retain their recorded constitution. Preview: Government's expanded participation, hearings, proposals, consent, and persistence have reopened acceptance work. Follow the installed edition's actual screens and current recorded decisions. In-game screenshot - Government Agenda: choose a matter on the left, read its stage, sponsor and proposal terms in the middle, and inspect member positions on the right. Record my position declares your choice; the scheduled decision comes later.

title: Authority and the ruler's limits
text: Government authority ranges from advice, through political pressure and reconsideration, to required approval for important decisions. At stronger levels the ruler may need a conscious override or a constitutional change; at the strongest level major actions can be blocked until approval is obtained. War, peace, treaties, policy, taxation, major spending, fiefs, and serious justice can fall within that authority. A valid military or diplomatic action is not permission to bypass Government. Relief and espionage have different classifications, but parties can still care about them. Increasing authority gives the institution a stronger role and brings public benefits. Reducing it through agreement differs sharply from forcing it down. Forced reduction can damage trust and relationships across the realm. An NPC's explicit consent protects only the person or clan they can actually represent, for the exact proposed change; it is not a permanent blank cheque.

title: Joining Government without a crown
text: You can read public records, prepare proposals, approach members, and seek support before holding a seat. Admission depends on the institution. A noble seat needs actual qualifying clan leadership and land. A civic mandate needs an eligible constituency, endorsements, and the supported adoption and decision process. If a seat is occupied, its holder does not lose it merely because you ask. Transfer consent or a lawful recall route may be required. Political sponsorship cannot invent an extra seat, give you someone else's vote, or make you a vassal by implication. A member can vote, support proposals, join political work, and seek party responsibility. Membership does not grant treasury access, military command, or a Royal Council seat. A title such as Senator describes a real recorded office, not permission to direct the kingdom.

title: Proposals, sponsors, parties, and sessions
text: Use Prepare a proposal and My Proposals where available. Choose the real kingdom, action or policy, target, and enactment or repeal terms. A draft is not a law. Changing its terms can require renewed support. In a supported conversation, Alt+A opens the action selector for political requests and the proposal route. Escape returns from the Government screen; inside the action builder it cancels that builder instead. Seek an eligible sponsor or party adoption. A willing member's personal support, a party's nomination, formal presentation, a vote, and actual enactment are separate stages. Speakers coordinate party work; they cannot turn their personal opinion into every member's ballot. An unused or unsupported nomination can expire rather than silently becoming law. Seats and future voting shares follow actual constituencies and territorial changes. A new holding can add representation; losing one can suspend it. Existing matters preserve their recorded voter roll rather than handing an absent member's vote to a newcomer. Crown and member weight also depend on the constitution, so do not assume every decision is a simple equal headcount. Diagram — Political route: draft, obtain support, secure adoption, present, vote, then verify enactment.

title: Hearings, recess, and political bargains
text: Public hearing speech enters the record but does not by itself spend gold, enact a policy, change a ballot, or create a private deal. Check attendance: absent members are not silently present in the conversation. For persuasion or a political bargain, speak with the actual available member in the supported individual conversation, including during a recess. There are no magical hearing buttons that guarantee a bought vote. Any accepted payment needs clear mutual terms, actual funds, and the right recipient. A deal depends on the promised obligation really being fulfilled. Political promises affect consideration; they do not guarantee every final vote. Read the recorded position and outcome. Changing your mind, missing a deadline, or failing an obligation can have consequences even if the original conversation sounded friendly.

title: Resolutions, edicts, and follow-through
text: Government business spans relief, food and agriculture, trade, security, defence, war and peace, raids, espionage, diplomacy, justice, construction, prisoners and households, and taxes or obligations. An edict or policy can benefit one area while burdening another. Read the current target, completion route, deadline, and tradeoffs. Paying money is not always the same as supplying goods or improving an actual settlement condition. A promising speech does not complete a resolution; check the requirement and whether the game recorded it as fulfilled.

title: Talking to the right authority
text: Rulers can negotiate war, peace, tribute, and longer agreements. NPC rulers also pursue their own policies according to personality, relationships, domestic pressures, current wars, and realm condition. You are not the only person capable of making the map change. A courtier can discuss an alliance without having power to grant it. An ambassador can negotiate only within their actual mandate. Ask who can decide, agree on the exact terms, and inspect the resulting agreement or native change. Use Alt+A in an eligible conversation to build a supported diplomatic action. For a written approach, open Correspondence with Ctrl+M , select the contact, then use Alt+A when the letter composer is ready. Political Pressure reflects friction or cooperation between realms and domestic lords. It can lead to peace, aid, trade, threats, or war. A ruler choosing foreign friendship may disappoint domestic supporters; supporting an angry noble faction may damage foreign relations.

title: What agreements can do
text: Supported diplomacy includes ordinary and tribute peace, reparations, settlement concessions, surrender, trade, non-aggression, alliances, defensive pacts, independence guarantees, prisoner exchanges, ransoms, hostage guarantees, border restraint, caravan protection, supply, loans or subsidies, paid neutrality, paid war entry, and dependent political arrangements. Compound packages can link several terms. Review who pays, who gives up territory or prisoners, which enemy is named, the duration, and whether it is public. Some arrangements directly alter Bannerlord state; others record obligations enforced when relevant events occur. A promise of supplies is not an already completed shipment. An incompatible war can break treaties and damage trust. Peace does not necessarily recreate an agreement that ended. Temporary Truce and Trade Embargo are retired legacy action names; use the supported alternatives instead of assuming those old labels execute.

title: Outbound and resident ambassadors
text: From Court's Ambassadors area, post an eligible ambassador, assign supported information, relations, or trade work, and recall them when appropriate. Postings occupy limited capacity and persist over time. A resident foreign envoy comes from another peaceful ruler to your capital. They travel, arrive, and reside there rather than appearing instantly. Capital movement can relocate the posting; war can recall it. An envoy's conversation and authority can pass to a successor without wiping the state's diplomatic history. An official envoy cannot grant something outside their charter, regardless of how persuasive you are. Refer an unauthorized request to the foreign ruler. Distinguish an ambassador's personal feelings from the terms they can officially approve. In-game screenshot - Ambassadors: your Foreign Advisor is on the left; foreign envoys have separate cards with their realm, location and travel status. Appointment, dismissal and Establish Relations are distinct controls.

title: Clan Accords
text: Preview: Clan Accords have source and contract evidence; their complete installed native lifecycle still needs acceptance. Clan Accords are smaller cooperative arrangements between the player ruler's clan and an NPC clan. They are not kingdom treaties. A lesser eligible adult noble can arrange an accord for their clan through explicit agreement; it does not always require the clan leader to negotiate personally. Use Alt+A in the ready conversation to find the supported Clan Accord action. Escape closes the Clan Accords management screen. Accord Practical benefit Trade cooperation A modest continuing income benefit Mutual Watch Better security in owned towns and castles Agricultural exchange Help with village household growth Artisan exchange Help with town prosperity Garrison cooperation Lower garrison wage burden Available slots grow with clan tier separately for each accord type. Benefits can stack, and a valid accord can begin helping new holdings acquired later. Review capacities, partners, arrangers, and benefits through the Economy entry beside the campaign date and its Clan Accords screen. Peaceful allegiance changes or an arranger's death need not end an accord. War with the partner's faction or clan elimination ends incompatible arrangements. Voluntary cancellation can hurt relationships; wartime termination has different rules. Peace afterward does not automatically sign them again. Accords can build goodwill but do not grant votes, military authority, or Spymaster access. Mutual Watch is cooperation, not a hidden unlimited intelligence-report service. Layout example — Clan Accords: inspect each partner and accord type, then confirm deliberately before cancelling.

title: Appointing and using a Spymaster
text: Appoint an eligible Spymaster, then use Court's Spymaster tab. Roguery matters, alongside the person's overall fitness for office. There are limited concurrent missions, and an officeholder with active work cannot simply be replaced to erase its consequences. Choose the mission, actual target, and shown terms. Read cost, duration, difficulty, and risk of detection before starting. A routine mission and an assassination are very different commitments. An unavailable target can invalidate work, and spent money is not automatically refunded. In-game screenshot - Spymaster: choose a mission tab, target and operation, read its assessment, then use Commit the Operation when ready. Reports and report details appear below; Archive is a separate tab.

title: Intelligence and sabotage
text: Intelligence work can investigate land, skills, relationships, rumors, and reputations. Counterintelligence searches for foreign agents. Sabotage can disrupt food contribution, construction, security, or loyalty for a period of time. Better expertise helps but does not guarantee success or secrecy. Important and well-protected targets are harder. Read the returned report: an attempt is not a successful disruption, and detecting activity is not always identifying its sponsor. NPC kingdoms can also disrupt food production in villages supplying an enemy town during wartime. This activity uses the NPC kingdom and runs alongside the Spymaster missions you choose. Its disruption wears off and food relief continues. Use Court's Economic Report to check food supplies when planning for a siege or shortage.

title: Social manipulation and lethal missions
text: Supported social work can mitigate your own or another person's damaging signal, promote a positive reputation, or fabricate harmful allegations. An allegation can affect society without making it objectively true. Established reputations are harder to erase than rumors. Assassination can kill a unique person and expose or capture your Spymaster. A captured operative can require ransom or a personal breakout attempt; rescue can fail and place you in custody too. Read those consequences before confirming. Counterintelligence and ordinary information work are available without choosing a lethal mission. Foreign realms can recruit disaffected agents and operate against you. A friendly-looking court is not proof that every member is loyal. Exposed agents leave the active hidden pool while their history remains.

title: Giving a clear campaign order
text: The Campaign Command Engine supervises accepted NPC party and army orders over time. It controls the commander's force, not your main party . You need legitimate authority or the commander's explicit agreement. Specify the commander, objective, target, duration or stop condition, and any troop or supply requirement. “Patrol around this town until I recall you” is different from “capture that castle.” A conditional reply or counteroffer changes the terms. Read the accepted version before confirming. Build the command with Alt+A in the supported conversation. For written orders or reports, open Correspondence with Ctrl+M and use Alt+A with the eligible commander selected. Orders can adapt to changing danger, war state, geography, and duties. A commander may report trouble, withdraw, refuse, or ask for guidance. Correspondence can carry those reports and their deadlines. Issuing the order does not mean it has already completed.

title: Campaign objectives you can combine
text: Aim Supported work Prepare Create the commander's party; recruit and resupply to agreed targets Travel Go to a named settlement or valid point; return home; withdraw to safety Hold and observe Hold until recalled or for a term; patrol; scout and report Coordinate Escort a party; form an army and wait; join, leave, or disband an eligible army Attack Raid a hostile village; besiege and capture a fortification; engage a named enemy; hunt enemies in a bounded region Defend Defend a settlement or relieve an active siege Multi-step orders can recruit, then patrol, then hold. Recruiting still requires funds and local manpower. Settlement surrender belongs to diplomacy, not a movement order disguised as a guaranteed capture.

title: War Council map and intelligence
text: Open Royal Court → Military → War Council . Inspect kingdom lords, parties, settlements, orders, and battle reports. Pan the map by clicking or dragging. It uses a fixed readable scale; the mouse wheel is not a normal zoom control. Your realm's parties are visible. Foreign parties depend on intelligence and can be missing because they have not been detected, not because they do not exist. The selected War Councilor's Tactics and Leadership affect intelligence; without one, the ruler supplies those skills. Drag supported orders onto valid map targets: Free Roam, Hold, Patrol, or Attack. An attack on a hostile village is a raid; an attack on a fortification is a siege/capture objective. Right-click Remove Order to clear a council order. A direct command already in force cannot simply be overwritten by an unrelated map gesture. Use the Raven control for correspondence when you need clarification or negotiated orders. Battle reports distinguish completed outcomes from current map positions, and naval battles/parties have their own presentation. Escape dismisses an open military-standing popup first; otherwise it closes War Council. The map orders use the mouse controls described above. In-game screenshot - War Council: the map is on the left, strength and reports in the middle, and Lords & Parties on the right. Peace Standing and War Standing are above the map; the settlement directory helps you find a location.

title: Peace Standing, War Standing, and garrisons
text: Preview: military standing and the revised war economy are actively being balanced and verified. Their goals are not a promised starvation timer or guaranteed food supply. The sovereign's Peace Standing and War Standing controls sit either side of the crowned R in the revised War Council. Automatic adjusts peace readiness to external pressure; a manual peace strength keeps your selected target. The Royal Docket's Kingdom Military Standing provides the corresponding orders. Peace standing limits automatic field recruitment. Peace drawdown selects eligible surplus healthy soldiers proportionally across troop tiers. This preserves more of the force's mix while the party shrinks. A safe subordinate lord party can release troops gradually. The main party, garrisons, heroes, and wounded troops are outside this drawdown. Current battles, army service, and a player-issued recruit and resupply order can prevent the drawdown. Released soldiers can help functioning village households recover. War standing still needs actual funds, recruits, and provisions. Garrisons keep defensive targets in either standing. Stationary garrison regulars cost less to supply and maintain than field troops; transferring them out returns them to field costs. Visiting parties do not gain that garrison discount.

title: Inviting a noble to travel with you
text: Ask an eligible noble from another clan to accompany you temporarily. This is a Temporary Party Guest agreement, not companion recruitment, vassalage, or a clan transfer. Agree on purpose, risk, and a fixed or open-ended term. The noble can refuse. Use Alt+A in the ready conversation to build the guest request or supported revision/departure action. To speak with a guest already traveling with you, open Party Chat with backslash (\) and select them. A guest retains clan, identity, and equipment; their equipment cannot be treated as freely available inventory. If they led a party, their real original force remains as [Name]'s Waiting Camp , protected while the noble visits. Do not mistake the camp for an abandoned army to harvest. At review, Speak Now opens the discussion and Let Them Depart begins the return. Departure can require actual travel back to the original party or a safe alternative. Asking them to leave early still requires the supported agreement; a polite farewell is not proof of departure. War with their faction forces a separate risk review. Letting a guest fight their own people can lead to banishment and a permanent clan change, subject to succession safeguards. Read that decision carefully; ordinary guest acceptance alone does not authorize it. Diagram — A temporary guest leaves a protected original party, visits under agreed terms, then returns through a recorded journey.

title: Choosing a duel
chapter: Duels, arrests, rulers, and civil war
text: An eligible NPC can agree to a duel in individual conversation. Read the Bannerlord Reign Duel prompt before starting; cancelling the start is different from losing a fight. Use Alt+A in the ready individual conversation to select the supported duel request and terms. Mode What is at stake Practice Private, nonlethal sparring. The opponent remembers it, but it does not produce ordinary public duel glory, disgrace, or automatic relationship rewards. Honor A nonlethal challenge whose outcome can enter public combat history, news, and reputation. Lethal A real death risk under the confirmed terms. Never treat it as ordinary practice. Nonlethal fights use protected health handling rather than normal campaign injuries. Duel training reduces health damage so combat can last longer while preserving a separate training-XP path; blocked hits can matter for learning too. It is not a way to apply those protections to an unrelated battle. The mission outcome decides who won. Narrating victory does not replace the fight. A duel used for an arrest has custody consequences and is separate from private practice. Existing native learning modifiers still affect actual skill gains.

title: Arrests: accusation, confirmation, and custody
chapter: Duels, arrests, rulers, and civil war
text: You need real jurisdiction: an eligible player-owned holding, an accused person in your party, or the supported encounter with their party. An insult in a distant conversation does not grant universal arrest power. Prepare an accusation with its reason, then explicitly confirm the arrest. These are separate steps. Reign considers cause and evidence; a serious unsupported accusation can hurt relationships and public standing. A rumor is not automatically a justified conviction. Use Alt+A for the supported prepare, confirm, release, or rescind action. Opening the selector does not itself order an arrest. During a party encounter, the accused can surrender or resist. A nonlethal arrest duel or native battle may follow. You gain custody only when the actual result places the person with you. Release frees the prisoner but retains the accusation. Rescind clears that accusation and its associated effect and releases the accused. Protected custody of your own realm's or clan's arrested people differs from ordinary random escape; deliberate release, death, and actual battle outcomes still matter. Diagram — Arrest has two decisions: prepare the accusation, then confirm; afterward release and rescind have different meanings.

title: Captured rulers and sovereign judgment
chapter: Duels, arrests, rulers, and civil war
text: Preview: expanded ruler capitals, capture protection, judgments, and settlement consequences have continuing native acceptance work. NPC rulers tend to remain at a secure capital until they can lead a substantial present army. They can relocate when a capital is lost and return after a campaign. These rules do not take away the player's freedom to travel. An army still approaching is not the same as soldiers already present. Defeating a ruler does not guarantee capture. When a sovereign is captured, the capturing sovereign has special decisions. A player vassal or mercenary does not acquire that sovereign power just by holding the prisoner; direct handover is distinct from a routine dungeon donation. Ordinary-war judgments can include an execution sentence, exile with concessions and a replacement ruler, or submission and annexation. Read the permanent political outcome and temporary settlement effects. Sentencing is not the same as actual death. During a pending sentence, normal sale or ransom cannot bypass it, but escape or rescue can cancel the pending outcome. An unauthorized vassal execution can anger both realms without granting the sovereign settlement package. The ruler feature also has life-and-death requirements; review its Options before assuming a no-death campaign preference will remain compatible. It changes no combat-death difficulty by implication.

title: Rebellion and civil war
chapter: Duels, arrests, rulers, and civil war
text: Disaffected NPC vassal leaders can begin a rebellion, and other clans choose sides. A non-ruling player vassal can also seek a rebellion through an accepted supported action. A promise of sympathy is not a clan transfer; a recruited lord must explicitly accept. A rebel realm is a real political faction. Capture, death, surrender, and rulership determine its decisive outcomes; an unrelated foreign power capturing a leader is not automatically victory for either civil-war side. Ordinary peace cannot simply skip the special resolution. Secret support for a future rebellion is distinct from joining one already declared. A pledge can bind a named clan to the challenge against a particular ruler while its current allegiance remains in place. Informers, refusals, summons, renunciation, and defiance can all become part of that political history. The later ruler-judgment flow distinguishes recognized rebel independence, execution under its sentence rules, and reunification under a victorious rebel leader. Loyalist victory can lead to freedom, imprisonment, or execution judgments for defeated leaders. These are substantial campaign choices and can affect the player as well as NPCs. Civil-war outcomes differ from ordinary conquest. Do not assume an ordinary-war annexation or settlement-effect package applies to a rebellion. Pending judgments and the sequence of decisions survive saving; inspect the remaining queue rather than assuming the first ruling resolved everyone.

title: Troops cost more than in native Bannerlord
text: Recruiting, upgrading, and maintaining a strong army is more expensive in Reign, especially as troops become more advanced. A field army that you can buy today may still be unaffordable to keep supplied. Native perks and discounts still matter; negotiated hero or guest pay follows its own agreement. Automatic recruitment and upgrading consider the actual payer's funds and future military obligations. Having spare kingdom wealth does not necessarily mean every clan can replenish. Manual player purchases still require real resources, without implying that every automatic safety buffer is a new player spending rule. Prisoner ransoms follow native valuation rather than inheriting the increased enlistment price. Releasing or selling prisoners is not a way to recover the full cost of building an elite force. Preview: current war-economy revisions have controlled and persistence evidence, but long-run balance and human acceptance remain open. Descriptions here explain the reviewed rules, not guaranteed outcomes for every kingdom. The higher wage base applies to regular troops in field parties and garrisons. The owned-party wage display accounts for that party's actual modifiers and discounts. Recruitment previews use the receiving party's forecast where available. Kingdom regulars cost a little more while their realm is at war with another kingdom and a little less at peace. This applies to both field and garrison wages after existing modifiers. Hero salaries, mercenary troops and companies, and independent clans are outside this particular adjustment. See War economy and clan trade settings to adjust the available cost rules.

title: Recruitment uses people, not an endless pool
text: New regular military recruits draw from eligible village households. Heavy recruitment leaves fewer people available and slows natural household growth for a while. A depleted or badly damaged village may be unable to supply more soldiers even when you have gold. This applies to player and AI recruitment and to supported automatic garrison and replacement-retinue routes. Existing soldiers are not retrospectively charged when the economy update arrives. Creating a new lord party does not grant a free fully funded army: its household troops depend on local people and actual money. Transferring soldiers, returning an expedition, upgrading an existing troop, or recruiting a prisoner is different from a new enlistment. Native mercenaries and special quest routes have their own handling. Civilian caravan and fishing crews do not consume village military manpower merely by being created or replenished. Diagram — Healthy villages support recruits and food; war losses, raids, and heavy enlistment strain that recovery. For automatic lord-party creation in NPC-ruled kingdoms, a noble clan generally needs land. Hired mercenaries can establish a party without land. Kingdom military support requires both land and an active serving lord party. Player-directed establishment and native initial or quest routes have their own rules. A landless household can still qualify for local stipends or civilian trade under Household stipends and NPC trade .

title: Household stipends and NPC trade
text: A landless NPC noble household with a verified permanent home may receive a small weekly stipend from the clan leader who owns that holding. Eligibility looks at the family's finances, the current owner, shared kingdom, and the payer's ability to keep a military reserve. To let your own clan participate, enable Fund Local Household Stipends in Reign's in-game settings. Payments use your personal gold. The installed land caravan pilot lets eligible landed and landless NPC clans sponsor standard caravans. Turn it on through Enable NPC Caravan Investment Pilot in Reign's MCM. It starts off and assigns a named captain. It charges the clan for both formation and working capital and checks that enough cash remains for military needs. The caravan trades and remits money through native Bannerlord. Loss can cost the clan its investment. Preview: the NPC Clan Trade revision has passed its Options browser checks and is awaiting final release validation. It adds land caravans and War Sails sea convoys with a suitable port. The sponsoring clan pays one formation fee and retains ownership and trade remittances. Bannerlord supplies the starting trade purse separately. New parties use merchant crews without assigning a named noble captain. Existing pilot caravans keep their captains and records. The separate land and sea controls are described in War economy and clan trade settings under the revision notice.

title: Raids, population, and recovery
text: Village households support production. Healthy larger villages contribute more, while devastation reduces actual output. A completed raid resets agricultural recovery; normal functioning and safer, better-fed conditions allow it to recover gradually. A raid's damage does not end when the smoke disappears. Several damaged villages can place separate security burdens on their linked town. Recruiting may remain restricted during early recovery. A village that is not functioning cannot be assumed to produce food or recover normally. Siege aftermath matters too. Mercy is less damaging to security than pillage or devastation. Choosing the harsher option has a continuing cost, not just a different line in the victory report. Raid damage now has its own food capacity measure alongside household recovery. Severe or repeated raids can shut down new food production. A functioning village recovers gradually, and low food or security slows that recovery. Open the Economic Report from Court to compare food capacity, household recovery, actual output, and healthy potential for the current population. In fishing villages, disruption reduces new catches from boats and shore facilities. Fish already carried remain in cargo. A working voyage can finish and unload. When the village's fishing capacity shuts down, boats unload before waiting ashore. Recovery allows another departure. Food shipments and relief use their own rules. Control Center → Options → War economy → Raid food disruption keeps recorded damage available for when you turn the rule back on.

title: Food markets, settlement stocks, and relief
text: Distinguish food offered in a market, food held by a settlement, food carried by an army, and cargo in transit. They are not the same stockpile. Threatened unsieged towns prioritize buying available food within their civilian budget. They cannot buy food that does not exist or spend unlimited money. Realm relief moves real food from eligible better-supplied holdings toward shortages while protecting donor reserves. It prioritizes serious projected need and loses some food along the route. Sieges can block purchases and deliveries. A manual shipment deducts stock when dispatched, takes time, and can be held outside a newly besieged destination while cargo deteriorates. Food traveling between holdings is not immediately available at both ends. Granary actions, normal market buying, automatic relief, and a court grant are separate mechanisms. Inspect the Economic Report's current reserve and projected trend before assuming a shipment solved a deficit. Relief can ease hunger without making a besieged or devastated realm self-sufficient.

title: Garrisons, patrols, and demobilization
text: Stationary garrison regulars have lower wage and food burdens than equivalent field troops. Native governor, culture, building, Billeting, and Clan Accord effects retain their own benefits and costs. A patrol or visiting army does not receive the new garrison reduction just for being nearby. Patrols use troops transferred from the home garrison. Replenishing them returns survivors before issuing another detachment. Removing a patrol outside combat returns its soldiers where supported; it does not create a fresh free roster. Peace drawdown can return some released manpower to functioning villages, while raids and mobilization strain still matter. It provides no automatic gold payout or instant prosperity. Keep defensive needs and actual household recovery in view when changing standing.

title: Battle medical discharge
text: Some regular soldiers newly wounded in battle can retire if they survive the battle without being captured and remain with the force they fought in. The result varies each battle. Better surgeon Medicine lowers the maximum possible loss. Previously wounded troops, captured soldiers, heroes, and civilian crews are outside this discharge rule. Rescue or release does not make a captured soldier eligible from the earlier battle. Eligible retired soldiers can contribute back to functioning village households. This is separate from peacetime release of healthy soldiers. See Peace Standing, War Standing, and garrisons for peacetime release. Medical discharge is installed. Individual battle and reload edge cases remain under review.

title: Ships, ports, and military purchases
text: Where War Sails is present, player ship purchases, repairs, and upgrades retain native pricing. NPCs retain their native discounted ship procurement. A cheaply procured NPC ship does not become a full-value resale windfall simply because it was transferred to a friend. Captured ships retain their separate normal native resale handling. Selling needs actual port funds. A sinking, discarded hull, or cleanup removal does not pay compensation. Governor commissions come from real eligible port business and cannot exceed the transaction. Existing ships without a known acquisition history use the documented migration handling instead of an invented past battle or purchase. Automatic military food and mount purchases in the payer clan's own realm still pay the market, but do not create an extra tariff payment back into that realm through the old loop. Ordinary trading and foreign purchases retain their own rules. This is a targeted accounting change, not a general abolition of tariffs.

title: A longer calendar and new-campaign differences
text: Reign's year and seasons last longer than native Bannerlord's, and character aging follows that calendar. Existing campaigns receive anchors so adopting the calendar does not suddenly change everyone's apparent date or age. Read the game's actual dates and agreed deadlines rather than counting native-length years from memory. New campaigns also include a deeper younger generation in eligible noble families and authored starting-age adjustments for Rhagaea and Ira. These are new-campaign setup changes; an update does not reseed children or overwrite ages in an established save. Newer narrative profiles likewise do not silently replace the life stories of old campaigns. Background world motion begins after the initial preparation grace period. Political incidents, court business, relationships, and rare kingdom events need actual campaign time. Waiting for a cloud response in a paused conversation is not the same as advancing the calendar.

title: Kingdom catastrophes and boons
text: These are occasional realm-wide events, with actual economic or political effects and later endings. They are not all variations of a generic prosperity bonus. Event What changes Famine / Bountiful Harvest Village food contribution falls / improves Pestilence / Population Boom Village households decline / grow Crime Wave / Law and Order Settlement security worsens / improves Trade Collapse / Trade Boom Prosperity declines / improves Construction Stagnation / Golden Age Building work slows / accelerates Political Unrest / National Unity Loyalty worsens / improves Border Crisis An eligible new war begins Grand Reconciliation An eligible ordinary war ends Orderly Succession An eligible NPC ruler gives way to a ruling-clan heir Effects persist for their recorded duration. A golden age speeds construction; it does not automatically grant every unrelated benefit implied by the phrase. Orderly Succession does not automatically retire the player ruler. The MCM catastrophe-and-boon switch controls new natural events.

title: News and announcements
text: Important diplomacy, ruler captures and judgments, kingdom-event beginnings/endings, and other eligible public outcomes appear through news. Ordinary captures do not all deserve a royal announcement. A sentence scheduled for later must be distinguished from an execution that has actually happened. The announcement screen pauses campaign time while you read and acknowledge it. Long reports scroll. Turning a popup category off changes presentation; it does not undo the war, judgment, or harvest. New reports also reach the normal text window, and re-enabling a category does not replay a cancelled backlog. After reading, Enter , Numpad Enter , or Escape acknowledges a ready announcement. These keys can resume the campaign after the report closes. Tournament news can reach the local social scene immediately, and team victories should credit the actual winning team rather than only the player. Firsthand participation, general public news, and a distant NPC's knowledge are still different things. Layout example — Diplomacy/news announcement: read the full report and confirmed consequences, then acknowledge to continue.

title: Arena Overhaul is included
text: Use Reign's single launcher module. Arena Overhaul retains its own Arena Overhaul MCM settings section and established saved preferences. Do not assume that all arena controls live under the Reign AI settings. The arena expands practice, loadout choices, companion participation, rewards, and tournaments. Talk to the arena master for the available practice routes. Fees, equipment options, and mode availability depend on those settings.

title: Practice modes and companions
text: Ordinary practice supports configurable participants, equipment, rewards, and experience. Expansive Practice broadens the exercise. Parry Practice focuses on defensive practice. Team Practice adds coordinated teams. Supported modes can let you play as a companion hero, and some can give viewing heroes experience when enabled. Choose loadouts and weapon preferences where offered. Preferred or more expensive loadouts can carry a fee; random equipment is different from buying that choice. Defensive equipment and team settings alter the practice setup rather than permanently donating those items to your party. These arena modes are separate from the keep's Training Yard and from a negotiated private practice duel. Use the one that matches whether you want to train troops, control a hero, practice a block, or spar with a particular NPC.

title: Tournaments and team victories
text: Tournaments can use broader prizes, prize quality and scaling, betting options, round rewards, and champion renown or influence settings. Team Tournaments have their own team-size and scoring controls. Reign's party-member team handling aims to let eligible accompanying heroes fight with you while keeping them out of opposing teams when you compete. A team win matters as a team result in history, reputation, and celebration dialogue. An NPC winner's monetary award is separate from player prize variety. Current economy work changes NPC award accounting without removing the player's normal prize choices. Preview: bundled arena integration, party-team eligibility, and the newest NPC reward revisions retain native acceptance follow-ups. Check the installed edition's available modes and do not treat an old design reference as a roster guarantee.

title: Participation XP
text: Meaningful completed spoken conversations can grant modest player Charm experience. Participating in a social-event phase can also provide a small learning bonus based on the actual people you spoke with. Deciding a real petition can grant Leadership experience. These are player participation rewards, not unlimited experience for opening windows, replaying a reply, or making the same person appear more times in a phase. Normal Bannerlord learning modifiers still apply. Control Center Options has an XP toggle plus overall and category adjustments. Conversation, event conversation, event learning, and petition rewards can be adjusted independently. Disabling a category does not bank old awards to reclaim when you turn it on again.

title: Portraits and Look at them
text: Reign can display persistent portraits across its own screens and supported native surfaces. Shipped characters can use the shared library; dynamic people and changed appearances can use campaign-specific pictures. A missing picture does not mean the person has no identity or history. Use portrait zoom for a larger view and Look at them for the supported appearance description and refresh choices. New portrait generation follows the configured image provider. It is separate from simply viewing a cached image. Current appearance and equipment matter, especially for encountered residents. A civilian's work clothes should not silently turn into noble costume just because a portrait was requested. Normal/adult image-profile settings and outfit changes have their own boundaries; they do not grant new gameplay authority. The shipped shared library is in the installed Reign module under PortraitCache/_shared . Campaign-generated portraits live in the managed ReignServer data/PortraitCache folder, grouped by campaign identity. Saves from the same campaign share that campaign's portrait folder.

title: View scenes and outfit previews
text: View in individual or Party Chat can request an illustration of the current scene. It uses the current conversation and relevant people as context; the resulting image can appear in the transcript and open larger. It is optional cloud image work, not an automatic screenshot of the native scene. An image can help you visualize a situation but cannot prove that a gift was delivered, a person arrived, or a battle occurred. If clothing is being changed, use the supported before/after preview and keep/revert choices rather than treating a generated picture as a completed equipment transfer. Castle scenes and Tavern House scenes have separate switches. Turning general portrait replacement off does not necessarily turn off every scene-image feature, and a scene may need portrait identity preparation even when native portraits remain visible elsewhere.

title: The Memory Book
text: Open Memory Book from the quest interface to browse illustrated memories. The book combines recorded experiences with optional artwork. Navigate the list and selected scene rather than expecting it to be a conventional quest objective list. An illustration is a visual interpretation of stored events. Changing or deleting a picture does not rewrite the original experience, promises, or world history. A fact can remain remembered without having an illustration. Layout example — Memory Book: choose a memory from the list and view its illustration and caption in the larger panel.

title: Small interface and native-behavior changes
text: Reign replaces supported main-menu logo/video presentation and uses its black-marble court style across major screens. It preserves usable native skill information, banners, and quest markers while hiding exact NPC relationship values. Narrated actions in supported conversation responses use italic treatment to help separate them from speech. The action builder's protected sentence has its own presentation. Neither formatting style means an action already happened. Reign-owned popups support consistent Enter/Escape behavior. Safety repairs also handle an encyclopedia interface disappearing during a tick, delayed native relocation races, and map-bar input during unavailable states. These are quiet stability changes rather than new player commands. NPC-owned settlement dungeons receive the same native prisoner-holding advantage as player-owned ones. Noble prisoners may therefore remain in AI custody more reliably. The foreign- governor loyalty penalty is removed by the ruler integration, while foreign ownership and matching-governor benefits retain their separate effects. Those two culture rules should not be confused.

title: A Bannerlord save and Reign memory belong together
text: Your native save holds Bannerlord's campaign. Reign also stores memories, relationships, history, images, and other campaign state in its local server. Save Sync pairs a protected native save with the matching Reign snapshot. Save with the server running. Reign prepares the matching snapshot and warns if the native save succeeds but server protection fails. An unprotected save is still a native save, but it is not proof that the matching Reign state is safely aligned. Restore service and make a new protected save rather than ignoring the warning. Copying or renaming a native save does not invent a fresh Save Sync identity. Loading an older protected point restores the associated Reign timeline; later memories should not bleed into an earlier world. Diagram — A protected save links Bannerlord state and Reign state; restoring an old point restores that matching pair.

title: Capacity and safe housekeeping
text: There is a limited pool of unique protected Save Sync states. Watch the warning and capacity display instead of keeping unlimited one-off saves and assuming every one is protected. Overwriting an ordinary rolling save can retire its older point where safe. Use the native save UI's supported deletion flow when removing a save you no longer need. Do not manually delete server database folders to make space. A native save can exist without its matching protected Reign point, and a renamed copy can still share the old identity. Keep intentional backups outside routine cleanup. Close Bannerlord before using the Control Center's Campaign Backups cleanup controls. Choose the individual campaign, campaigns with no matching saves, or the full cleanup option, then answer the Are you sure? prompt. The no-save cleanup preserves campaigns with matching physical saves, imports awaiting their first load, and the shared portrait library. Full cleanup removes Reign histories, backups, campaign portraits, and related queued work. The native save files and installed shared portraits remain. An already scheduled cleanup can finish after the server starts.

title: Exporting and restoring a campaign
text: In Campaign Backups , select the correct campaign and export its archive. Keep the matching native Bannerlord save with it. The Reign archive preserves campaign-side memory and supporting data; it does not contain your global provider API keys. On restore, select the intended archive and inspect any replace-existing-campaign warning before confirming. Loading a native save from one point with unrelated server data is not a complete restoration. Keep a separate copy of the current pair before replacing anything valuable. Deleting a Reign campaign is destructive even if it leaves the native save file behind. Deleting all campaigns is broader still. A backup, a protected snapshot, an older native save, and a new campaign are four different things.

title: Updating, moving computers, and removing the mod
text: Before a major update or move, export Reign campaign data and retain the matching native save and package/version information. The installation's module, writable cache, selected server environment, and shared portrait library have deliberate locations; copying only a DLL is not a complete installation. Existing campaigns keep established identities and profiles unless an explicit supported migration changes them. Do not assume a new-campaign feature will be retrofitted. Likewise, do not assume removing a mod with saved campaign behaviors mid-campaign is supported. This guide does not claim a tested universal uninstall or cross-version save-conversion path.

title: Which settings window to use
text: Use MCM inside Bannerlord for game-side feature and execution switches. Use the Control Center for providers, server-side gameplay options, images, memory, backups, and advanced diagnostics. Arena Overhaul has its own MCM section. Use the installed launcher's managed server on/off and Control Center controls. An ordinary browser tab or an old batch-file instruction is not necessarily the supported lifetime owner for your installed edition. Do not close or restart the server during an important request or save unless you are deliberately recovering from a problem.

title: Execution and server connection switches
text: Execute Diplomacy Actions , Execute Strategy Plans , Execute Internal Politics Actions , and Execute Conversation Actions determine whether their supported plans may create real game effects. Enable Campaign Command Engine governs persistent NPC orders. Enable Ruler-Driven NPC Diplomacy enables autonomous foreign-ruler work. Use Local Bannerlord Reign Server , Local Server URL , and Receive Server Action Commands connect the native game with its server. A working chat with action execution turned off can still produce discussion without the transfer or order you expected. Correct the relevant setting deliberately; do not enable every debug control as a general repair. The utilities Open Party Chat and Open Correspondence provide alternatives to backslash (\) and Ctrl+M . Alt+A opens actions within a supported, ready Reign conversation rather than globally on the map. Show Debug Messages is informational; Enable Debug Controls exposes tools that can change a campaign or generate provider work. They are not required for ordinary play.

text: Area When an ordinary player needs it General / launcher controls Confirm server health and open its managed controls LLM Backend and Models Configure the cloud dialogue account/provider and model routes AI Image Generation Configure the separate cloud image provider and portrait options Options Participation XP, correspondence pacing, news, approaches, NPC Lives, ruler-related choices, and other exposed gameplay preferences Campaign Backups Save Sync status, export, import, and confirmed campaign deletion Characters Advanced inspection or correction of a person's record and portrait variant Character Memory Memory search and advanced retrieval/consolidation maintenance Prompting / Castle Chat Customize supported dialogue, room, image, and event prompts Diagnostics / Logging / Log Viewer Find a failed operation or collect a useful report Audit Viewer / Conversation Diagnostics Inspect a selected conversation's processing; captured payloads can include private campaign context Action Router Advanced action routing and diagnostics World History Inspect recorded world events and their chronology NPC Lives and Story Editor Advanced story definitions, prompts, timing, and Approach model controls under Diagnostics Test and lab areas Developer/acceptance tools, including Dialogue Lab, Relationship Director, World Test, Test Lab, Live Test Bridge, and Verification Lab Test tools can alter state or consume provider allowance. They are not a way to unlock the normal game. Character Editor revisions can change a campaign and may have native effects; inspect the exact change and confirmation rather than treating it as an in-character ability.

title: War economy and clan trade settings
text: In the Control Center open Options , then War economy . You can adjust troop wages, recruitment and upgrades, village food output, garrison wage and food savings, automatic spending reserves, and raid food disruption. A disabled group keeps the values you entered. For wages and upgrades, change the cost rules. For garrisons, change the stationary wage and food savings. Spending reserves protect money needed for upcoming obligations. The Fund Local Household Stipends switch is in Reign's in-game MCM. Preview: the NPC Clan Trade group is in the upcoming revision. Its Options checks passed and deployment awaits release validation. Land caravans and War Sails convoys have independent enable switches, formation prices, and per-clan active limits. Both start off. The shared cash setting caps the fee as a share of clan cash, and the daily chance applies to eligible clans after affordability and reserve checks. Turning a mode off or lowering its limit changes future launches. Existing parties continue trading.

title: Provider choices, costs, and privacy
text: Keep cloud dialogue and cloud image configuration separate. A provider can be configured yet temporarily unavailable, out of allowance, or unable to serve the selected model. Use the supported saved route and its diagnostic feedback. Cloud requests send relevant game/conversation context to the selected provider. API keys remain server-side rather than entering the Bannerlord client. Reign's local memory worker does not mean dialogue never leaves the computer. Optional external vector storage has a different role from the dialogue provider; raw campaign prose is not simply the vector itself. Turn detailed conversation capture on only when you need it and understand what is stored. Logs and exported diagnostic payloads can contain private fictional character information and your own chat text. Avoid sharing a whole settings file when a redacted error and selected report will do.

title: Chat is slow or not answering
text: Check that the launcher-managed server is healthy, the selected cloud LLM provider is configured and available, and the game points to the installation's correct local URL. Initial character preparation can take longer than a warm conversation. A long cloud response does not prove your graphics card is too weak. Keep the pending operation's status in view. Reopening may recover a result already being generated. If the request clearly failed, use its retry path; do not send many copies of the same request or change every provider setting at once. If reporting it, keep the error, approximate time, NPC, conversation surface, and relevant diagnostics.

title: The NPC agreed, but nothing happened
text: Check the attached action or agreement status, execution settings, actual target, funds, inventory, ownership, presence, authority, and safety. The accepted terms may involve a future date or physical travel. A new counteroffer can mean you have not yet accepted the final version. For a guide, follow them. For a departing guest, allow the return journey and inspect the agreement. For a government proposal, check adoption and the actual vote rather than its draft. For a shipment, check cargo and access. These are different failures and should not all be fixed by repeating “yes.”

title: A menu, person, or picture is missing
text: Check eligibility first. Court needs rulership and appropriate location; a full Royal Court needs a capital. Homes lists known available residents. Party Chat uses available eligible people. A pregnant NPC may be withdrawn. An ambassador can still be traveling or recalled. For pictures, distinguish cached display from new generation. Check Enable AI Portraits and the relevant scene switch, then the separate cloud image settings. Missing optional artwork should not be treated as a missing character. A Preview feature may also differ between the reviewed source and your installed package.

title: Saving warns, preparation stalls, or a rollback seems wrong
text: Keep the native save. Read whether it is protected or unprotected, whether capacity is full, and whether the server is reachable. Re-establish the matching services and use a protected save or known matching backup pair. A successful native save alone does not establish that all Reign data was captured. Use preparation Retry for a recorded failed stage. Do not delete database folders or invent a new campaign to bypass a recoverable stage. If an older save appears to know future events, preserve the save and diagnostic evidence and report a timeline-alignment problem rather than continuing to overwrite your only good pair.

title: Quick glossary
text: Term Meaning Native Bannerlord's own game systems, before Reign's extra behavior MCM Mod Configuration Menu inside the game Control Center Reign's local settings, campaign, and diagnostic interface LLM The cloud language model generating the AI's words and structured responses Image provider The separately configured service generating optional new artwork Reign server Local companion service connecting game state, memory, and providers Directional relationship How one person feels about another; the reverse can differ Rumor An uncertain, usually temporary social allegation Reputation A more established public conclusion Public Standing The combined social effect of current public signals Political Pressure Realm/ruler political tension or cooperation, separate from Government Government The kingdom's representative institution, members, parties, and authority Clan Accord A limited cooperative arrangement between clans, not a kingdom treaty Docket Court's pending business and recorded decisions Chancellor The separate salaried petition-delegation office Royal Council Specialized advisors; their advice does not execute an order Receipt / recorded result Evidence that a particular operation actually committed Save Sync The link between a native save and its matching Reign state Timeline The restored branch of campaign history belonging to a save point Preview Implemented behavior with outstanding acceptance or installation uncertainty

title: What is still being verified
text: The guide covers the reviewed code and documented behavior, not a claim that every feature has passed release acceptance. Significant open areas include Royal Council, expanded Government participation and hearings, broader court-life work, NPC Lives journeys and missions, residents/Homes recruitment, personal gossip/communications, Clan Accords, Tavern House, ruler judgments, arena integration, and recent military/economic balance. Descriptions of these areas explain what their implemented routes are for, while Preview notices flag their limits. A roadmap checkbox, a successful build, a picture, and a natural-sounding reply are each different from final native acceptance. Your installed edition can also lag behind current development source. The manual's maintenance files retain topic-to-source coverage, source hashes, illustration provenance, and Claude/Grok/Gemini review notes. They help update the guide when the mod changes. Hardware planning figures remain provisional until representative campaign measurements are available. This edition covers the reviewed action sentence catalog and the marriage and economy changes through November 9. The local installation includes the revised NPC matchmaking, Nord households, medical discharge, and war economy rules. The wedding evidence covers one complete Aserai route. The controlled war economy observations cover specific routes, with broader campaign balance still being tested. Preview notices indicate an edition difference or an open acceptance check. The NPC Clan Trade notice states its current deployment status.
